name: The short end of the stick

meaning.zh:
“吃亏” 或 “受到不平等对待”。

这个短语起源于古时候的斗殴或争端，人们常用棍子来评判谁该受到责罚或怪罪。有时候，有人会故意给一方一根很短的棍子，以表示他在争执中不占优势或者受到了不公平对待。渐渐地，这一短语就被广泛用于形容人们在某件事情中吃亏或受到不平等待遇。
meaning.en: This phrase originates from olden days when sticks were used in fights or disputes to judge who should be punished or blamed. Sometimes, a very short stick would be given to one side to symbolize that they were at a disadvantage or being treated unfairly. Over time, this idiom has come to be widely used to describe people being in a situation where they are at a disadvantage or unfairly treated.

lines.en: I really got the *short end of the stick* in that deal.
lines.zh: 在那笔交易中，我确实是吃亏了。

lines.en: She always seems to get the *short end of the stick* at work.
lines.zh: 她在工作中似乎总是受不平等对待。

lines.en: If you don't ask for what you deserve, you'll end up with the *short end of the stick*.
lines.zh: 如果你不争取应得的东西，你最终会吃亏的。
